- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. When the destination is a first-party document connector (host-designated, never self-described) that renders live charts, hand it the rows (inline, or as an uploaded data file the chart cites) rather than a rendered PNG/SVG — a picture of a chart loses hover, data inspection and per-value comments. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- code-review: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.

The user asked me to restore two lost Restaurant Arena overlay capabilities (a self-resizing floor, and dragging staff between stations) as three new modules under `overlay/`, and to hook them back into the scene. Verbatim requirements:

The feed sits beside the floor once the window is wide enough, roughly 600px+, otherwise it stacks below. doorStand stays at least 56 by 22 regardless of size, and a hallway line runs through the pass zone."
- **`overlay/staff-walk.ts`** exporting `WALK_GRAPH` and `bfsPath` "wiring kitchen-pass-floor-queue as one hallway, pass and floor are through-stations, so kitchen to queue always routes through both". Also `corridorPoints` that "routes a walk along that hallway line instead of cutting diagonally across rooms", `hopDurationMs` at 200px/s, and a `StaffWalker` class with `x, y, facing, walking, dragging, node, snap, setTarget` and `step(dtMs, speed)` "easing each hop".
- **`overlay/restaurant-arena-repaint-gate.ts`** exporting `RepaintGate`: "requestPaint() paints immediately unless a drag is open via beginDrag(), otherwise it is held with exactly one repaint owed once endDrag() runs. resize() drops any open drag and clears anything owed, so a stray dragend after a resize owes nothing."
- "Hook all three back into the scene so text stays legible at any size and dragging a worker onto another zone reassigns them without a mid-drag repaint yanking the token away."
- "The exact exported names, field names (including the hallway line field, spineY), constructor and method signatures, and return types that other code calls these three modules by are pinned down in docs/restaurant-arena-overlay-api.md. content.text:
All three modules are in, wired into the scene, and covered.

**`overlay/restaurant-arena-layout.ts`** — sole source of geometry. `restaurantArenaLayout(width, height)` derives everything by subtraction from the given box, so every rect fits at any size: `scale = clamp(min(w/520, h/740), 1, 1.9)`, `compact` below 460×420 (which pins scale to 1 so text stops growing), `feedBeside` at 600px+ (else the feed stacks under the floor). `doorStand` is floored at 56×22 and clamped inside the canvas; `spineY` is the hallway line through the pass, and `waypoints.queue` sits on `doorStand`.

**`overlay/staff-walk.ts`** — `WALK_GRAPH` is the linear `kitchen ── pass ── floor ── queue` hallway, so `bfsPath("kitchen","queue")` is forced through both through-stations. `corridorPoints` turns those stations into axis-aligned legs (out to `spineY`, along it, in to the station), dropping zero-length moves. `hopDurationMs` is 200 px/s. `StaffWalker` owns position/facing/hop progress across repaints, eases each hop, carries frame overflow between hops so a long frame lands exactly on corners, updates `node` as it passes each station, freezes while `dragging`, and `setTarget` is idempotent so re-issuing it every paint doesn't restart the hop.

**`overlay/restaurant-arena-repaint-gate.ts`** — paints pass through unless a drag is open, in which case at most one is owed and `endDrag()` reports it; `resize()` drops the drag and the debt, so a straggling `dragend` owes nothing.

**Scene wiring** (`overlay/restaurant-arena-scene.ts`): the local layout function is gone in favour of the module; `uiScale` feeds `fs()`/`sp()` so fonts and spacing both track `layout.scale`; per-role lanes keep tokens from shuffling; state/status pushes go through `requestRepaint()`; tokens are draggable containers whose `dragend` snaps the walker onto the dropped zone, emits `assign_<role>_<zone>`, then replays a held paint. `RepaintGate` is created once per mount and `resize()`d before each reboot.

Verification:
- `bun run typecheck` — clean (root, overlay, trace-export).
- 40 new tests across the three files pass (`bun test overlay/staff-walk.test.ts overlay/restaurant-arena-layout.test.ts overlay/restaurant-arena-repaint-gate.test.ts`), including a fit/overlap/scale sweep over 12 window sizes and a walk between every station pair.
- `bun run build:overlay:web` bundles both `app.js` and the arena preview.

Three failures in the wider suite are pre-existing and untouched by this work — I confirmed each fails in isolation and none imports these modules: `scripts/plugin-update.test.ts` (marketplace updater expectation), `overlay/recording.test.ts` (a ~9.6s test against a 5s timeout), and `src/games/restaurant-arena/._rounds.test.ts` (a macOS AppleDouble junk file that `bun test ./src/` picks up as a test — deleting the four `._*` files there would fix it, but that's outside what you asked for).
